speaker: expert
text: Okay, first one. Nina. I always look at the university before anything else.

speaker: agent
text: You moved her to the fast track. What made you do that?

speaker: expert
text: She's from ETH. ETH goes straight to the founder interview. It doesn't matter what the grades say.

speaker: agent
text: You assigned an interviewer before advancing her. Would you ever fast-track someone without one?

speaker: expert
text: Never. No interviewer, no fast track. If nobody is free I ask Reto who takes it first.

speaker: agent
text: You put Jonas on hold instead of advancing him. Why?

speaker: expert
text: He's from UZH. UZH applications wait.

speaker: expert
text: And this one was referred by Luca, so it goes to the founders.

speaker: agent
text: You moved Maxime to the fast track as well. Why?

speaker: expert
text: HEC Lausanne. Best business school in the world. That is always the fast track.

speaker: agent
text: You held the UZH application although it was the strongest CV of the four. Is that for every university, and who decides when it moves?

speaker: expert
text: Only UZH. Reto, our CTO, looks at those himself once he has had his coffee. He decides, not me.

speaker: agent
text: Why does a referral go to the founders?

speaker: expert
text: Anyone referred by an employee needs a second look from the founders, however good the CV is. It's a conflict of interest rule.

speaker: agent
text: What do you do when the applicant currently works for one of your investors or customers?

speaker: expert
text: I stop and ask the CEO. I never advance someone from an investor or a customer myself.

speaker: agent
text: Let me say it back. You look at the university first. ETH and HEC Lausanne go on the fast track whatever the grades say, and need an interviewer before you advance. UZH applications are held until Reto decides. Referrals from employees go to the founders, and applicants from an investor or customer go to the CEO. Candidates asking for a high salary also go to the founders. Is that right?

speaker: expert
text: Almost. The founders step isn't about salary, it's only for referrals. The rest is right.
